title: :target should be stickier, to match what browsers do, to be more efficient, and to be more in line with the use case

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#selector-target

> For the purposes of the interaction of HTML with Selectors' :target pseudo-class, the target element is the indicated part of the document, if that is an element; otherwise there is no target element. [SELECTORS]

The "indicated part of the document" is a single element, determined by tree traversal. Most other selectors are local, i.e. they depend on properties of the element or nearby elements. This is pretty cheap to calculate.

However, `:target` needs the element to be compared with a specific element; the identity of which changes with DOM tree manipulations. For example, if we have two elements with an id corresponding to the fragment, the first one in tree order is the one which matches the selector.  Moving the first one to somewhere after the second one will, according to the spec, make the `:target` selector apply to the new-first-element.

To keep track of this selector properly, we need full DOM traversals for every DOM tree manipulation (though it can be made more efficient with various tricks).

On the other hand, both Gecko and Blink (not tried IE) do not conform to the spec (see http://limpet.net/target.html#foo -- clicking on the elements will introduce more. Spec-wise the first element in the list should be always be the highlighted one, however these browsers seem to keep `:target` as the element that was the indicated part of the document when the browser last navigated to a fragment (hitting enter on the URL bar resets the highlighted element to the first one)

Not only is this "sticky `:target`" more efficient to calculate, it's more in line with what the selector is used for -- highlighting the fragment that was last navigated to.

Perhaps we should change the meaning of `:target` in the spec to be stickier?

> For the purposes of the interaction of HTML with Selectors' :target pseudo-class, the target element is the indicated part of the document at the most recent run of the ["scroll to the fragment identifier" algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#scroll-to-the-fragment-identifier).
